stem: A hospital observes that a common bacterial infection is no longer responding to the previously effective antibiotic. What would be the best strategy to address this issue?
Differentiate between narrow-spectrum and broad-spectrum antibiotics.
keyPoints: ["Narrow-spectrum antibiotics act against a limited range of bacteria.","Broad-spectrum antibiotics act against a wide range of bacteria.","Penicillin and tetracyclines are canonical examples respectively."]
modelAnswer: Narrow-spectrum antibiotics act against a limited variety of bacteria; penicillin is an example. Broad-spectrum antibiotics act against a wide range of bacteria; tetracyclines are an example.

stem: Discuss any two major groups of antibiotics.
keyPoints: ["Bacteriostatic antibiotics inhibit bacterial growth.","Bactericidal antibiotics kill bacteria.","Sulphonamides, tetracycline, and cephalosporin are named major groups."]
modelAnswer: Two major antibiotic groups are bacteriostatic antibiotics, which inhibit bacterial growth, and bactericidal antibiotics, which kill bacteria. The chapter also names sulphonamides, tetracycline, and cephalosporin as major groups of antibiotics.
